_note: Versioned policy constants for bounded orientation reads. These are the ONLY authority for orientation size bounds — no checker, schema, doc, or test may carry its own literal. Exceeding any limit is a fail-closed refusal with stable reason code orientation_too_large; nothing is ever silently truncated. Raising a limit is a reviewed policy change that advances limits_version and owes a release-ledger entry.

max_source_bytes.applies_to: The total bytes of orientation source read from Git objects at the target OID: release ledger, changelog, supported surface, and orientation contract data files.
max_source_bytes.rationale: 1 MiB. Measured at surface 1.13.0 the whole set is about 22 KB, so this is roughly 45x current headroom while still bounding a single read to something a consumer can hold in memory and hash without streaming.

max_section_count.applies_to: The number of changelog sections an orientation window may reference between the reviewed baseline and the target commit.
max_section_count.rationale: 8 sections existed at surface 1.13.0 across roughly one month of releases. 64 covers several years of the same cadence in one window, while still refusing an unbounded full-history narrative loaded into model context.

max_section_bytes.applies_to: The bytes of any single changelog section body.
max_section_bytes.rationale: 64 KiB. The largest section at surface 1.13.0 was 3.9 KB, so this is about 16x headroom. A single section larger than this is a drafting error, not a release worth orienting on in one read.

max_envelope_bytes.applies_to: The serialized orientation envelope handed to the consumer.
max_envelope_bytes.rationale: 256 KiB. Roughly 64k tokens worst case, which keeps a full orientation read inside a model context budget with room for the session's own work. Deliberately smaller than max_source_bytes: the envelope is a selection of source, not a copy of it.

max_ledger_entries.applies_to: The number of release-ledger entries an orientation window may carry between the reviewed baseline and the target commit.
max_ledger_entries.rationale: The ledger holds 1 entry at limits_version 1.0.0. 256 bounds the window without forcing an amendment-heavy history to be re-baselined early; a consumer that exceeds it should adopt a newer reviewed baseline rather than read further back.
